Backend: 7/7 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_backlog_lokl_prefix.py — (a) LOKL- order id prefix on a fresh OTP-driven order matches ^LOKL-[0-9A-F]{8}$ (e.g. LOKL-XXXXXXXX), (b) the new order is retrievable via GET /api/orders/{id}, (c) legacy BFO- ids in admin feed still look up cleanly, (d) POST /api/admin/complaints/INVALID-ID-XYZ/resolve now correctly returns 404 (regression from iter-20 silent-200 fixed at server.py:3352-3353), (e) a valid open complaint still resolves 200 with {ok:true}, (f) GET /api/v1/cities/bhilai returns eta_config + max_delivery_radius_km, (g) /api/v1/cities/detect classifies Delhi vs Bhilai correctly. Frontend: 4/4 location-banner specs pass (Delhi coords → banner with exact spec text 'We don't deliver to your area yet — you're browsing Bhilai for now.'; X-icon dismiss sets lokl_loc_banner_dismissed_v1=1 and persists across hard reload; Bhilai coords → banner hidden; missing lokl_loc_v1 → banner hidden). Dynamic ETA hook verified: in-footprint Bhilai coords yield 21-45 min ETAs across 10 cards (base 15 + 4×km, matches eta_config), out-of-footprint Delhi coords fall back to static 45-90 min — NO 3,600+ regression. Admin regression: 9/9 tabs (Overview/Live/Merchants/Bank-Address/Stores/Products/Orders/Returns/Customers) load with zero console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: LocationBanner uses GET /api/v1/cities/detect on every (lat,lng) change with no debouncing — fine today because lat/lng only changes when the customer regrants location, but if a future GPS-tracking feature streams updates, add a 1s debounce.

useCityConfig.cache is a module-level Map with no TTL — eta_config will not refresh until the tab is closed. Acceptable for a config that changes server-side rarely; flag if delivery pricing tiers ever need a live-bust.

Out-of-footprint detection in useDeliveryEta caps at max_delivery_radius_km and falls back to static minutes. Note the per_km calculation uses straight-line km from the card's `store_distance_km`; if the backend distance computation is haversine, in-city ETAs are slightly optimistic. Not a correctness bug.
Order id LOKL-{8 hex chars} → uuid.uuid4().hex[:8].upper() yields ~4B unique ids. At ~250 orders so far the collision probability is negligible; raise to 12 chars if volume ever exceeds 1M orders/yr.
